own_solution.law: Newton's second law for each block plus rotational dynamics of the pulley (I = M R^2/2, no-slip a = alpha R): a = (m2 - m1) g / (m1 + m2 + M/2)
assumptions: pulley is a uniform solid disc rotating about its centre
system released/moving freely with no other external forces

TFE1B.regime: Irrelevant while both string tensions stay below the 200 N breaking strength; here T_left = 3(9.8+2.178) = 35.9 N and T_right = 5(9.8-2.178) = 38.1 N, far below 200 N.

TE857.regime: Irrelevant while both tensions (about 35.9 N and 38.1 N) remain below the 200 N limit.

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: A frictionless pulley axle is not stated, though it is the standard default and needed for the closed-form answer.

notes: Base: a = (5-3)(9.8)/(3+5+2/2) = 19.6/9 = 2.1778 m/s^2. With 0.8 kg added to the left block (glued or tied beneath, both move with it): a = (5-3.8)(9.8)/(3.8+5+1) = 11.76/9.8 = 1.2 m/s^2; right block still heavier, so the direction is unchanged. Radius cancels: torque (T2-T1)R = (M R^2/2)(a/R) gives T2-T1 = M a/2, independent of R. Breaking-strength sentences are K: max tension about 38.1 N (about 37.6 N with the extra 0.8 kg) is well below 200 N. Shelf block is D. Variant groups: {TB39A, TA3B0, TA3AE} all state 0.8 kg and differ in attachment (R, R, D); {TDDE2, TFF18} both state 12 cm radius ('from axle to rim' equals radius); {TFE1B, TE857} both state 200 N ('break only above 200 N' vs 'withstand up to 200 N' are equivalent statements of the same threshold). All variants consistent in number and unit.
